HR & Operations Manager
1. Role Overview
We are looking for a proactive, responsible and execution-oriented HR & Operations Manager who will independently manage the company's HR functions and oversee operational effectiveness and project delivery across all departments.
The individual will be responsible for ensuring that employees, teams, processes and projects function efficiently, without unnecessary delays or operational bottlenecks.
This role involves managing the complete employee lifecycle, coordinating departmental operations, monitoring project delivery, maintaining internal processes and driving continuous organisational improvements.
We are looking for someone who identifies what needs to be done, takes ownership, independently drives initiatives and ensures that things are implemented rather than simply communicated.
The expectation is to take ownership of people, processes and delivery, without waiting for instructions.
2. Key Responsibilities
A. Human Resources Management
Take complete ownership of the company's HR functions, including:
Manage end-to-end recruitment, from identifying hiring requirements to sourcing, screening, interview coordination and onboarding.
Coordinate employee onboarding, induction and offboarding.
Maintain employee records, attendance, leave management and HR documentation.
Develop and implement HR policies, employee guidelines and internal procedures.
Monitor employee performance, productivity, attendance and accountability.
Coordinate performance reviews, feedback sessions and employee development initiatives.
Handle employee grievances, workplace concerns and internal communication.
Ensure employees understand their roles, responsibilities and performance expectations.
Plan employee engagement activities and initiatives to improve workplace culture.
Support workforce planning based on departmental requirements, project pipelines and upcoming resource needs.
Identify HR-related issues and proactively resolve them.
B. Operations & Department Coordination
Take ownership of the company's internal operational efficiency and ensure smooth coordination across all departments.
1. Department Coordination & Workflow Management
Coordinate with all departments to ensure ongoing client projects and internal tasks progress without unnecessary blockers.
Regularly follow up with department heads and team members on pending tasks, deliverables and dependencies.
Identify operational bottlenecks, resource constraints and communication gaps.
Proactively escalate blockers to relevant stakeholders and ensure timely resolution.
Ensure delays and unresolved issues are identified before they impact client delivery.
Monitor interdepartmental coordination and ensure teams work towards common organisational goals.
Ensure responsibilities, task ownership and deadlines are clearly assigned.
2. SOP Development & Implementation
Ensure every department has clearly documented and updated Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Coordinate with department heads to identify gaps in existing processes.
Ensure SOPs are documented, reviewed, communicated and implemented.
Regularly monitor adherence to established processes.
Identify processes that are inefficient, outdated or unnecessarily complicated.
Drive standardisation of workflows across departments.
3. Process Improvement & Operational Excellence
Identify opportunities to improve employee productivity and organisational efficiency.
Independently propose and drive initiatives to reduce manual work, unnecessary processes and operational delays.
Improve internal communication, reporting structures and workflow management.
Identify opportunities for automation and better utilisation of existing tools and systems.
Work with department heads to implement improvements.
Monitor the effectiveness of implemented initiatives and ensure measurable improvements.
C. Project Delivery & Workforce Monitoring
Take responsibility for maintaining visibility over day-to-day project progress and ensuring that operational issues do not affect timely project delivery.
Monitor day-to-day project delivery, timelines, milestones and operational progress.
Ensure projects follow agreed workflows, SOPs and internal processes.
Work closely with Project Managers, Product Owners, Developers, QA teams and other department leads.
Track project progress and identify delays, resource gaps, dependencies and delivery risks.
Ensure project responsibilities, deliverables and ownership are clearly assigned.
Identify projects at risk of missing deadlines and coordinate corrective actions.
Follow up with relevant teams to ensure pending deliverables and operational issues are addressed.
Monitor staff productivity, workload distribution and resource utilisation.
Support recruitment and workforce planning based on upcoming project requirements.
Escalate critical delivery risks to management with appropriate recommendations.
Note: The role involves monitoring and coordinating project delivery, rather than independently managing the technical execution of projects. Department heads and Project Managers remain responsible for their respective project deliverables.
D. Internal Accountability & Management Reporting
Ensure departments follow established reporting and communication practices.
Monitor completion of internal operational initiatives and pending action items.
Coordinate internal meetings, reviews and operational follow-ups.
Maintain visibility over operational issues and ensure they are closed within reasonable timelines.
Prepare regular management reports covering:
Employee headcount, attendance and performance.
Recruitment status and workforce requirements.
Department-wise resource capacity and utilisation.
Project health, progress and delivery timelines.
Pending tasks, operational blockers and delivery risks.
Process improvements and implementation status.
Present relevant operational concerns and improvement recommendations to management.
3. Expected Working Approach
The ideal candidate must demonstrate:
Initiative: Identify what needs attention and take action without waiting for instructions.
Ownership: Take responsibility for ensuring initiatives are completed.
Problem-solving: Identify root causes and recommend practical solutions.
Proactiveness: Anticipate potential operational, employee and delivery-related problems.
Coordination: Effectively work with different departments and stakeholders.
Accountability: Follow through on tasks until the intended outcome is achieved.
Continuous Improvement: Consistently look for ways to make the organisation more efficient.
Execution: Convert identified problems and proposed solutions into actual implementation.
This is not a role where the individual simply follows instructions, sends reminders or reports problems.
The expectation is to independently identify, coordinate, implement and close issues.
4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Performance will be evaluated based on:
HR & People Management
Recruitment turnaround time and successful hiring.
Employee onboarding and HR process completion.
Timely resolution of employee-related concerns.
Employee attendance, performance monitoring and documentation.
Effectiveness of workforce planning and resource allocation.
Operations & Process Management

Project Delivery & Reporting

Legal Content Specialist (LLB)
This role sits between our legal reality and our readers. CookieYes publishes a large library of privacy content that businesses across the world rely on to understand what the law asks of them, and we need someone professionally qualified to stand behind it.
We are looking for a law graduate who writes because they want to, not because a brief demanded it. You will track privacy legislation across jurisdictions, translate it into content our customers can act on, and act as the internal check on the legal accuracy of everything we publish and ship. Part of the role is genuine legal work: reviewing our own agreements, supporting compliance queries from customers, and keeping our product claims defensible.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Monitor privacy and data protection developments globally, including GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA and other US state laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, PDPA and emerging regulations, and flag what matters for CookieYes and our customers.
Write authoritative long-form content: regulation explainers, jurisdiction guides, compliance checklists, legal update posts and whitepapers.
Act as the legal accuracy reviewer for marketing and product content, with an agreed turnaround SLA so reviews never stall the pipeline. Nothing that makes a compliance claim should ship without your reading.
Structure that content to be found and cited by AI search, AI Overviews and answer engines, working with the SEO and AI search team on generative engine optimisation, schema and citation-worthy formatting.
Translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, working with product and engineering on how consent, records and disclosures need to behave.
Support customer-facing compliance queries escalated by sales and support, and build the internal reference material that reduces how often they need escalating.
Review and maintain our own legal documents, including the privacy policy, terms of service, DPAs and vendor agreements, with external counsel where required.
Prepare briefing notes for leadership when a regulatory change affects roadmap or positioning.
Represent CookieYes’s point of view publicly through bylined articles, webinars and industry commentary.
REQUIREMENTS
LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognised institution. Enrolment with a bar council is welcome but not required.
2+ years of relevant experience in a law firm, in-house legal team, compliance function or legal publishing role.
Demonstrable writing ability outside pleadings and contracts. Send us published work, a blog, a newsletter or a substantial piece written for a non-lawyer audience.
The instinct to write for a business owner rather than a bench. Accuracy without legalese.
Working familiarity with data protection law, or clear evidence you can master a regulatory area quickly and thoroughly.
Fluency with AI tools for research, drafting and summarisation, paired with the discipline to verify every citation, holding and date against the primary source before it reaches a draft.
Research discipline: you cite primary sources, you check whether guidance has been superseded, and you do not build an argument on a secondary summary.
Sound judgement about the line between explaining the law and giving legal advice, and the care to keep our content on the right side of it.
GOOD TO HAVE
A privacy certification such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US or CIPM, or the intent to pursue one, which we will support.
Prior experience at a SaaS, privacy tech or legal tech company.
Experience drafting or negotiating DPAs and SaaS agreements.
Comfort with SEO, GEO and how legal content performs in traditional search, AI search and AI Overviews.
Additional language ability relevant to EU jurisdictions.
Good understanding of, or familiarity with, major global privacy and data protection laws, including GDPR, CCPA, DPA, PDPA, UCPA, and related regulations.

job_title: AI Search & Agentic Growth Specialist (LLM SEO)
job_description:
AI Search & Agentic Growth Specialist (LLM SEO)
A growing share of the people who need a consent management platform now ask an AI assistant instead of a search engine. They ask ChatGPT how to comply with GDPR, they ask Claude to add a cookie banner to the site it just built, and they read an AI Overview instead of clicking a result. CookieYes intends to be the answer in those places.
This role has two halves. The first is AI search visibility: getting CookieYes recommended, cited and integrated across LLM surfaces. The second is agentic automation: building the AI workflows that let a small growth team operate like a much larger one. We are looking for someone who is genuinely hands-on with both.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Own CookieYes’s visibility in AI search: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Google AI Overviews. Define how we measure it, then improve it.
Build the measurement layer for LLM visibility: prompt sets, share-of-voice tracking, citation monitoring and competitor benchmarking, so this stops being anecdotal.
Run generative engine optimisation in practice: content structure, entity and schema markup, extractable formatting, and the freshness signals that make a page quotable.
Identify which third-party sources LLMs cite in our category, and work with content, PR and partnerships to earn placement in them.
Work with product and partnerships on distribution inside AI ecosystems, including MCP servers, connector directories and plugin marketplaces, and on integrations with AI website builders.
Build agentic workflows for the growth team: competitor and regulation monitoring, content research and briefing pipelines, review and approval flows, reporting automation, and internal tooling that removes manual work.
Evaluate and integrate AI tooling across the growth stack, and set the guardrails: what gets automated, what stays human-reviewed, and how we check output quality.
Keep the traditional SEO fundamentals intact. AI search sits on top of technical health, internal linking and topical authority, not instead of them.
Report on AI-sourced traffic, assisted signups and share of voice, and tell the team plainly what is working and what is noise.
REQUIREMENTS
3+ years in SEO, content strategy or growth engineering, with demonstrable recent work on AI search, GEO, AEO or LLM visibility.
Hands-on experience building agentic workflows or automations with tools such as n8n, Zapier, Make, LangChain, or direct API and MCP integrations.
Working knowledge of prompt engineering and LLM behaviour, including retrieval, grounding, citation patterns and why models hallucinate a competitor’s name.
Solid technical SEO foundation: crawling, indexing, structured data, site architecture and Core Web Vitals.
Comfort writing scripts. Python or JavaScript at the level needed to pull APIs, parse results and build a monitoring job.
The instinct to build measurement before making claims. This field is full of confident assertions with no data behind them.
Clear written communication, and the honesty to say when an AI channel is not yet worth the investment.
GOOD TO HAVE
Experience with MCP servers, AI connector directories or plugin marketplace listings.
Familiarity with tools such as Ahrefs Brand Radar, Profound, Peec AI or similar AI visibility platforms.
Background in B2B SaaS, developer tooling or a technical product category.
Experience with digital PR or link earning as a route to citation.
Understanding of privacy and compliance as a subject area.

Affiliate Marketing Manager
Affiliates are CookieYes’s largest partner-driven acquisition channel and the one with the most room left in it. We are hiring an Affiliate Marketing Manager to set the strategy for the program and then run it: recruiting, activating and scaling a global base of publishers, agencies, developers, newsletter operators and content creators.
This is an operator role with a clear number attached. You will own affiliate-sourced paid signups and the revenue behind them.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Build the strategy for the affiliate program: which partner segments to pursue, which geographies and platforms to prioritise, what the commission and incentive model should be, and what the program needs to look like at three times its current size.
Own affiliate recruitment: identify, pitch and onboard publishers, review sites, agencies, YouTube creators, newsletter operators and niche communities in our category.
The metric that matters is not affiliates signed up, but affiliates producing revenue. Own the journey from signup to first conversion, including repeat revenue and retention or reactivation.
Design and iterate the commission structure, including tiered and performance-based models for high-volume partners, testing new approaches and incentives, while benchmarking competitor affiliate programs to keep CookieYes’s commissions, attribution model, incentives and overall partner proposition competitive.
Manage the program day to day on platforms such as Tapfiliate or PartnerStack, including tracking, attribution, approvals and payouts.
Equip affiliates: creatives, landing pages, comparison content, product briefs, demo assets and campaign calendars.
Run affiliate-specific campaigns around launches, seasonal moments and regulatory deadlines.
Police quality. Monitor for brand-bidding violations, misleading claims, coupon abuse and fraudulent traffic, and enforce program terms.
Report weekly on signups, conversion rate, revenue per affiliate, activation rate, retention and payout efficiency, and act on what the numbers say.
Work with content, design and the growth team to produce assets affiliates actually use, and to fold partner content back into our own channels.
REQUIREMENTS
2+ years running or supporting an affiliate, partner or performance marketing program, ideally for a SaaS or subscription product.
Hands-on experience with an affiliate platform such as Tapfiliate, PartnerStack, Impact, ShareASale or similar.
Familiarity with building and managing influencer partnerships across channels such as Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn, X (Twitter), newsletters, and other relevant platforms, with an eye for repurposing and integrating influencer content into existing growth channels such as organic, paid, social, and content marketing.
Comfort with tracking and attribution mechanics: cookies, postbacks, coupon codes, and deduplication against other channels.
Strong outbound and relationship skills. A large part of this job is cold outreach that does not read as cold.
Analytical rigour in spreadsheets, and the judgement to spot a channel that looks good but is cannibalising organic.
Clear written English for partner communication, newsletters and program documentation.
Bachelor’s degree in marketing, management or a related field.
GOOD TO HAVE
Experience automating partner onboarding, payouts and engagement workflows.
Experience in a WordPress, Shopify or other CMS plugin ecosystem.
Exposure to paid affiliate or co-funded ad programs.
Basic SEO knowledge, enough to judge the quality of an affiliate’s traffic.

Global Partnerships Manager

We are hiring a Global Partnerships Manager to build that layer. You will identify, negotiate, launch and grow integration and distribution partnerships across international markets, and you will work as closely with our product and engineering teams as you do with partner business teams.

Growth Lead
CookieYes is a consent management platform used by over a million websites to stay compliant with GDPR, CCPA and a growing list of global privacy regulations. We are a product of Mozilor, and we sell to business owners, agencies and developers in more than 100 countries through a product-led motion and a fast-expanding marketplace and partner network.
We are hiring a Growth Lead to own the full customer lifecycle: acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention. You will write the growth plan, own the budget behind it, and be accountable for the number it produces. This is not a coordination role. You get real spend, a team to build, and the authority to decide what we try next, and in exchange we expect a high rate of shipped experiments and a straight answer every week on what worked.
We are looking for someone who has done this at scale before, in a SaaS business past $10M ARR, and who runs the ship without being asked twice.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Own the growth plan and its implementation. Set quarterly targets across acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention, sequence the work, and be accountable for shipping it rather than presenting it.
Own the numbers end to end: signups, activation rate, free-to-paid conversion, cohort retention, churn, expansion revenue and CAC payback.
Acquisition: lead across organic, paid, product-led, AI search and marketplace channels, and decide where budget and effort go each quarter.
Onboarding: own the path from install to a live consent banner. Work with product to cut steps, reduce drop-off, and get every new user to first value fast.
Engagement: build the lifecycle programme across email, in-app messaging and in-product prompts that brings users back into the product and deepens usage.
Retention and churn: track cohort retention, diagnose where and why accounts leave, run win-back and reactivation, and take the structural fixes to product and support.
Expansion: drive upgrades and plan movement through usage-based triggers, and design and analyse pricing and packaging tests with product and finance.
Build and run the experimentation roadmap across the website, onboarding, pricing page, in-app upgrade paths and lifecycle email.
Build the growth reporting layer. Define the metrics that matter, instrument them properly, and make the numbers legible to the wider team.
Partner with the Global Partnerships and Affiliate teams so that channel growth and self-serve growth reinforce each other rather than compete.
Manage and mentor a small team of specialists across performance, lifecycle, SEO and AI search, and hire into gaps as the team scales.
Own the paid budget: allocate it across channels, defend the allocation with data, and reallocate the moment the data changes.
Run a weekly growth review: what was shipped, what moved, what we are killing.
OWNERSHIP AND WAYS OF WORKING
You will own the number. Not contribute to it, not support it. If growth is behind, it is your call what changes and your job to say so early.
Experiment velocity is a standing expectation, not a stretch goal. We would rather run ten tests and lose six than deliberate for a quarter and ship two.
You will not be handed a backlog. You are expected to find the constraint yourself, decide what to do about it, and start.
Decisions get made with the data available, not the data you wish you had. Speed of iteration beats precision of planning here.
You will have real budget and the authority to move it. That comes with the obligation to report honestly when it is not working.
Small team, no layers, direct access to leadership and product. Nothing about this role requires waiting for permission.
REQUIREMENTS
4+ years in growth, performance or product marketing, including direct growth ownership at a B2B SaaS business at $10M+ ARR scale.
Evidence you have moved a company-level number at that scale. Tell us what it was when you took it, what you changed, and where it ended up.
Full-lifecycle ownership, not acquisition alone. We want to hear about a retention, onboarding or expansion number you moved, not only a channel you scaled.
Experience owning a substantial paid acquisition budget, including the decision to cut spend that was not paying back.
A track record of running experiments at volume, with a system for prioritising them and the discipline to kill losers quickly.
Experience turning a growth plan into a sequenced roadmap and delivering against it quarter after quarter.
Strong command of funnel and cohort analytics. You are comfortable in GA4, Mixpanel or Amplitude, and you pull your own data rather than waiting on someone else.
Hands-on paid acquisition across Google Ads, Meta and LinkedIn, and the judgement to know when to switch a channel off.
Working knowledge of SEO and content-led acquisition, enough to direct specialists and judge quality.
Experience building lifecycle and in-product messaging programmes in tools such as HubSpot, Customer.io, Intercom or similar.
Statistical literacy. You know what a valid test looks like and you do not call results early.
Experience hiring, managing and holding a small team to account.

Lock Desk Analyst – U.S. Mortgage
Job Description: Lock Desk Analyst – U.S. Mortgage
Job Summary
The Lock Desk Analyst manages mortgage rate lock requests, pricing, lock changes, extensions, relocks, and cancellations according to company policies, investor guidelines, and market pricing. The role involves coordinating with Loan Officers (LOs), Loan Processors (LPs), Secondary Marketing, underwriting, and investors to ensure accurate pricing, timely lock execution, and compliance with established procedures. The analyst also reviews daily investor rate sheets, maintains pricing accuracy in mortgage systems, investigates and resolves pricing discrepancies, and supports the smooth functioning of the mortgage lock desk.
Key Responsibilities
1. Mortgage Rate Lock Management:
Process rate lock requests from Loan Officers (LOs) and Loan Processors (LPs), verify loan details (amount, program, interest rate, LTV, FICO, occupancy, property type, and lock period), ensure eligibility and compliance with company policies and investor guidelines, and accurately process new locks, changes, extensions, relocks, and cancellations on time. Monitor lock expirations, communicate confirmations, rejections, and required corrections, and maintain accurate records in the loan origination system.
2. Mortgage Pricing and Rate Sheet Management:
Download and review daily investor rate sheets for dates, pricing adjustments, product availability, and lock periods. Upload and maintain rate sheets and pricing data in the pricing engine. Compare investor pricing with internal systems to identify differences. Review base pricing, loan-level price adjustments (LLPAs), margins, concessions, discount points, and lender credits. Calculate and verify final borrower or broker pricing according to company policies. Provide accurate pricing information to Loan Officers for eligible loan scenarios.
3. Lock Extensions, Relocks, and Pricing Exceptions:
Review and process lock extensions, relocks, and pricing exceptions according to company policies. Calculate extension fees, relock fees, and pricing adjustments. Check lock history, expiration dates, previous extensions, and available free extension days. Process pricing concessions and exceptions only after obtaining the required approvals. Verify approval authority and maintain supporting documents. Communicate applicable fees, pricing impacts, and processing restrictions to the requesting teams.
4. Investor Guidelines and Product Eligibility:
Review investor guidelines and product eligibility before processing lock requests. Verify delegated and non-delegated lending channels, where applicable. Confirm product availability based on loan program, credit score, occupancy, LTV, loan purpose, and other applicable criteria. Identify investor-specific restrictions and escalate exceptions when needed. Coordinate with investor representatives to resolve pricing, eligibility, and lock-related issues. Ensure all pricing and lock activities follow investor requirements and internal policies.
5. Communication and Issue Resolution:
Respond to inquiries from Loan Officers, Loan Processors, Secondary Marketing, and other internal teams. Explain pricing differences, lock rejections, extension fees, and investor restrictions clearly. Follow up on pending lock requests, pricing exceptions, and unresolved system issues. Escalate complex pricing and eligibility concerns to the appropriate manager or authorized approver. Maintain professional communication and meet established service-level agreements (SLAs).
6. Quality Control and Reporting:
Maintain accurate records of lock requests, confirmations, extensions, relocks, cancellations, and pricing exceptions. Check loan details and pricing for accuracy. Prepare daily or periodic reports on lock activity, expiring locks, pending requests, and pricing issues. Follow internal controls, audit requirements, and documentation standards.
Required Qualifications
A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field is preferred.
At least 1 year of experience in U.S. mortgage operations, Secondary Marketing, or mortgage rate lock desk operations is preferred.
Knowledge of mortgage pricing, rate locks, extensions, relocks, cancellations, and Conventional, FHA, VA, USDA, and applicable Non-QM products is required, along with Excel, Microsoft Office, and pricing analysis skills.
Strong analytical, numerical, problem-solving, and communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple requests under tight deadlines are essential.
Key Competencies & Performance Metrics
Strong analytical, numerical, and problem-solving skills.
Accuracy in mortgage pricing, rate locks, extensions, and relocks.
Good time management, prioritization, and attention to detail.
Effective communication, teamwork, and knowledge of investor guidelines and compliance requirements.
Timely processing of lock requests, quick resolution of pricing issues, and adherence to company policies and service-level agreements (SLAs).
Accurate documentation, audit readiness, and reduction of processing errors.
Work Schedule & Location

job_description:
Love talking to people? Obsessed with great products? This one's for you.
Company: Offrd (Sequoia AT) – AI-powered HR platform for Indian businesses
Location: Trivandrum / Kochi / Chennai
Experience: Freshers welcome! (0–1 year experience)
Role type: Full-time, customer-facing
Ready to start right away? We’re looking for a sales enthusiast who can jump straight in and drive this role forward with passion and energy.
Why this role is different
Most entry-level jobs bury you in tickets and targets. This one doesn't. You'll be the face and voice of Offrd — an AI-powered HR platform used by hundreds of Indian businesses. Your job is simple: talk to customers, show them what our product can do, help them succeed, and build relationships that last.
The workload is light. The impact is not. You'll get direct exposure to the founder, real customers, and real business decisions from day one — the kind of learning that takes years in a big company.
What you'll actually do
• Be the voice of Offrd — run product demos on Zoom/Meet, welcome new customers, and make them feel at home.
• Chat, call, connect — answer customer questions over calls and chat, and turn confused users into happy fans.
• Show off the good stuff — introduce customers to premium features and help them see the value in upgrading.
• Network like a pro — build genuine relationships with HR and business owners across India.
• Be the customer's champion — pass feedback to the product team and help shape what we build next.
Who we're looking for
• A natural people person — you genuinely enjoy conversations, not just tolerate them.
• Excellent communicator — fluent, confident spoken English (Hindi is a big plus for our North Indian customers).
• Dynamic and self-driven — you don't wait to be told; you spot opportunities and go after them.
• Product-passionate — you love exploring apps, understanding how they work, and explaining them simply.
• Calm under pressure — when a customer reports a problem, you solve it with a smile, not a panic.
• Fresher or up to 1year of experience — in customer success, sales, support, demos, or anything people-facing. Attitude matters more than your resume.
One honest thing you should know
Our customers are business owners and HR teams — and they sometimes need us in the evenings or on weekends. So this role needs someone happy to take a call or reply to a chat outside 9-to-6 hours. In return, the overall workload is genuinely light, and we're flexible with you too. If you see "always reachable, rarely overloaded" as a fair trade, we'll get along great.
What's in it for you
• Fast-track learning: work directly with the founder and core team of a growing SaaS startup.
• Real ownership: your customers, your relationships, your wins.
• A career springboard: this role grows into customer success leadership, product, or growth roles.
• A product people actually use: see your work make a difference for real businesses every single day.

job_description:
About the role
We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus of the role is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements as needed, alongside supporting existing entities and reinsurance programmes where required. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build-focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady-state reporting.
Key responsibilities
Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) — defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, and ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet the requirements of the relevant regulator; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g. DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
Build the financial model for each new entity — three-statement model and entity-level profit and loss — establishing the management reporting suite from which ongoing reporting will run.
Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring the accounting treatment and control framework are correctly set up from inception; support existing programmes as required.
Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity-level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing the format, commentary structure and distribution; support the ongoing production of these for existing entities as required.
Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) — providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for completion of the annual capital setting process (ECM/SBF cycle), optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining the FAL headroom analysis relative to the approved capital requirement.
Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities — including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity — to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes — including letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits — ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed in line with programme terms and regulatory requirements.
Own the capital waterfall and inter-entity funding mechanics — managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, and ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
Produce the board-level capital reporting pack — including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes — on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, including covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day-to-day work.

Qualified or finalist accountant (ACCA, CIMA, ACA or equivalent).
Experience with capital adequacy and solvency reporting, regulatory returns, and capital stress testing within an insurance or reinsurance context; familiarity with SCR/MCR frameworks across more than one jurisdiction is an advantage.
Hands-on financial modelling experience, ideally within insurance or reinsurance.
Understanding of reinsurance accounting (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission) and collateral management arrangements (letters of credit, trust accounts) supporting reinsurance programmes.
Demonstrable experience setting up the financial and reporting infrastructure for regulated entities in one or more of: DFSA/DIFC, Cayman Islands, Lloyd’s of London. Familiarity with Lloyd’s capital processes — including FAL management, the ECM/SBF annual cycle and Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) structures — is a strong advantage. Comfortable working independently.

Polus provides identity and contact data to enterprise clients through APIs and bulk delivery. A background in any one of these fields is sufficient; a combination of all three is not required. Mindset matters most.

Identify the fears, doubts, beliefs and motivations that influence how different engineer personas respond to AI.
Help document behavioural patterns and translate assessment findings into actionable insights.
2. Understanding How People Think – Cognitive Science
Study how engineers learn, interact with and use AI tools in their daily work.
Explore when engineers trust, question, resist or ignore AI-generated outputs.
Identify patterns in learning, decision-making and problem-solving that influence AI adoption.
3. Behaviour Change & Intervention – Behavioural Science
Help design and implement persona-specific interventions to improve AI adoption.
Support experiments and practical initiatives that encourage consistent AI usage.
Track behavioural changes over time using observations, feedback and usage data.
Compare outcomes before and after interventions and recommend improvements based on the findings.
4. Research-to-Action & Reporting
Convert observations into clear hypotheses that can be tested using data.
Support the implementation of research findings
Document results, identify what works and what does not, and communicate clear, decision-ready conclusions.
Refine approaches when evidence shows that an intervention is not effective.

Cognitive Science

Action-oriented: Moves from findings to implementation without waiting for perfect information.
Evidence-driven: Relies on observed behaviour, feedback and usage data rather than opinions alone.
Outcome-focused: Measures results, draws clear conclusions and recommends the next steps.
Adaptable: Accepts when an approach does not work and changes direction based on evidence.

Ability to explain research findings in simple, practical terms.

Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced Technical Project Manager to take ownership of project planning, technical team coordination, client communication, and end-to-end software delivery.
The successful candidate will act as the primary coordination point between clients, developers, testers, technical leads, and company management. The role requires a strong understanding of software development, the ability to manage multiple projects, and the confidence to drive accountability across teams.
The candidate must be proactive in identifying risks, resolving coordination issues, managing priorities, and ensuring that project commitments are met. They should be capable of independently managing day-to-day project execution while keeping management informed of progress, risks, and decisions requiring attention.
This is a hands-on project delivery role, not merely an administrative or reporting position.
Key Responsibilities
1. Project Planning and End-to-End Delivery
Take ownership of assigned software development projects from requirement clarification through development, testing, release, and ongoing maintenance.
Work with clients and technical teams to understand business requirements, scope, priorities, and expected outcomes.
Convert requirements into actionable tasks, milestones, delivery plans, and realistic timelines.
Estimate and coordinate effort, resources, dependencies, and delivery schedules with technical leads.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously while ensuring priorities and commitments remain clear.
Track planned versus actual progress and take corrective action when projects deviate from agreed timelines.
Ensure deliverables meet agreed requirements and acceptance criteria.
Manage scope changes, assess their impact on timelines and resources, and obtain appropriate approvals.
Maintain clear ownership of deliverables, outstanding actions, and upcoming milestones.

Coordinate developers, QA engineers, technical leads, and other stakeholders to ensure smooth execution.
Understand technical discussions involving application architecture, databases, APIs, integrations, defects, hosting, and deployment.
Work with technical leads to assess estimates, identify dependencies, and evaluate delivery risks.
Review task progress and ensure developers provide timely and accurate updates.
Identify technical blockers and facilitate their resolution.
Challenge unrealistic estimates or commitments constructively and help establish achievable delivery plans.
Coordinate code reviews, testing, bug fixes, release preparation, and deployment activities.
Ensure development work follows agreed priorities, coding practices, and quality processes.
Monitor workload distribution and raise resource constraints or competing priorities with management.
Foster accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement within the technical team.
3. International Client Communication and Relationship Management
Serve as the primary day-to-day project contact for assigned international clients.
Communicate professionally with clients, including those based in the United States and Europe.
Lead project meetings, progress calls, requirement discussions, sprint reviews, and delivery reviews.
Provide clear and regular updates on completed work, current progress, upcoming deliverables, risks, and pending decisions.
Clarify requirements and ensure client expectations are translated into actionable technical tasks.
Manage client feedback, change requests, approvals, and dependencies.
Communicate potential delays early, explain their impact transparently, and propose corrective actions.
Manage expectations regarding scope, effort, priorities, and delivery commitments.
Handle project concerns and disagreements professionally, escalating significant commercial or strategic matters when necessary.
Maintain accurate records of client discussions, decisions, commitments, and action items.

Maintain accurate project plans, task trackers, milestone schedules, issue logs, and risk registers.
Monitor task completion, overdue items, unresolved defects, and pending client inputs.
Prepare regular project status reports for management and clients.
Track project health, delivery risks, resource dependencies, and schedule deviations.
Identify warning signs early and initiate corrective actions before issues affect delivery.
Ensure every significant issue has a clearly identified owner, target resolution date, and follow-up plan.
Escalate critical risks promptly with relevant facts, potential impact, and recommended next steps.
Maintain visibility into the status of all assigned projects so management is not surprised by preventable delays.

Track outstanding bugs, severity, resolution progress, and client acceptance.

Support incident coordination and prioritization when production issues affect clients.

Improve visibility into developer workloads, project progress, delivery commitments, and pending decisions.
Identify gaps in project ownership, communication, estimation, and execution.
Develop practical standard operating procedures and reusable project templates.
Use project management tools and AI-assisted productivity tools to improve reporting, documentation, meeting summaries, and workflow efficiency.
Review recurring delivery issues and implement corrective measures.
Recommend improvements to resource utilization, development workflows, quality processes, and client communication.

Highlight decisions requiring management intervention, together with recommended options.
Support project prioritization and resource allocation discussions.

job_description:
About
NeedStreet builds the ContinuousCare cloud platform that healthcare organisations use to deliver care online. Healthcare businesses run their own branded patient experience on our multi-tenant B2B SaaS platform. The services we run are critical to patient care, so we treat security, privacy and reliability as core product features.
Role Overview
We are looking for a Senior AWS DevOps Engineer to own the reliability, security, and delivery of our B2B SaaS platform on AWS. You will be responsible for cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, container platforms, observability, and security compliance, and you will work closely with application engineering teams.
Responsibilities
Cloud Infrastructure (AWS)
• Operate and secure production infrastructure across EC2, VPC, ALB, WAF, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, ECR, IAM, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Athena, and Secrets Manager / SSM.
• Manage networking, edge routing, web application firewall rules, and TLS/certificate lifecycle.
• Carry out capacity planning, performance tuning, and cost optimisation.
• Own backup, restore, and disaster recovery procedures and testing.
Infrastructure as Code
• Design and maintain Terraform modules, state, and environment configuration.
• Run infrastructure changes through code review and CI, and handle configuration drift.
Kubernetes & Containers
• Design, provision, and operate Kubernetes (EKS) clusters and workloads.
• Build and maintain secure, efficient container images and runtime configurations.
CI/CD
• Own build, test, and release pipelines (GitHub Actions), including artifact versioning, environment promotion, approvals, and rollback.
• Integrate security scanning (images, dependencies, secrets, IaC) into delivery pipelines.
Platform Services
• Operate and tune Redis, RabbitMQ, MySQL, Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth2), and Apache/nginx reverse proxies.
• Support the deployment and runtime operation of Java (Spring Boot / Spring Cloud) and Node.js services.
Security & Compliance
• Apply least-privilege access, secrets management, encryption, network segmentation, and system hardening.
• Support compliance programmes (e.g., SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, GDPR) through audit evidence, access reviews, logging and retention, change management, and vulnerability management.
• Lead incident response and post-incident reviews.
Observability
• Maintain metrics, logging, and alerting with Prometheus/Grafana, Loki, CloudWatch, and OpenSearch/Kibana.
• Write and maintain runbooks and operational documentation.
Automation & AI
• Automate operational tasks with Bash, Python, and/or PowerShell and the AWS CLI/SDKs.
• Use AI-assisted tools responsibly, in line with data protection and security policies.
Collaboration
• Act as a technical point of reference on infrastructure and delivery practices, and mentor other engineers.
Required Qualifications
Candidates must have hands-on production experience in each of the areas below.
• 6+ years in DevOps, SRE, or cloud infrastructure engineering, including 4+ years running production workloads on AWS.
• Terraform at production scale: module design, remote state across multiple environments, CI-driven plan/apply, and drift and state management.
• Kubernetes in production, preferably EKS: cluster provisioning with Terraform, Helm/Kustomize, ingress, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies, upgrades, and troubleshooting.
• Ownership of CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions preferred).
• Deep Docker expertise, including multi-stage builds and image hardening.
• Production operation of Redis, RabbitMQ, and MySQL.
• Apache and nginx as reverse proxies.
• Operating JVM (Spring Boot / Spring Cloud) and Node.js services in production.
• Keycloak or a comparable OIDC/OAuth2 identity platform, from an operations perspective.
• Prometheus/Grafana, Loki, and OpenSearch/Kibana.
• Security-first engineering: IAM design, secrets management, encryption, audit logging, and vulnerability management.
• Experience supporting compliance audits (SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, or similar), ideally in healthcare or another regulated-industry SaaS.
• Strong scripting in Bash plus Python or PowerShell.
• Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools with appropriate security controls.
• Clear written and verbal communication.

job_description:
Position: NOC / SRE Lead – NOC Operations
Location: Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India (Onsite)
Experience: 8+ Years
Employment Type: Full-Time
Department: Network Operations Center (NOC)
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced NOC / SRE Lead to own the health, observability, and incident response for a connected fleet of field-deployed systems and the data center infrastructure that supports it.
This is the keystone L3 role in our Network Operations Center (NOC). You will own deep diagnosis and root-cause analysis on the running system, command the hardest escalations, and build the standards, runbooks, observability architecture, and operator-certification program that the rest of the NOC inherits.
As the L3 Lead, you will act as the escalation point above L2 support teams, taking ownership of the most complex incidents while keeping escalations to L4 product engineering limited to genuine code and firmware issues — protecting both fleet uptime and engineering velocity.
This is a greenfield opportunity. In the near term, the role combines a hands-on L3 technical function with NOC leadership. As the NOC scales, the role is designed to grow into a Principal SRE or NOC Manager track.
Key Responsibilities
1. Fleet Health & Observability
Architect the monitoring stack the NOC runs on — scrape architecture, alert rules, dashboards, and SLOs — rather than only consuming it.
Own end-to-end visibility of the connected fleet across data center, edge Kubernetes, Linux, and network layers.
Continuously tune alerting to reduce noise and catch degradation early.
2. Data Center & Infrastructure Operations
Oversee the health and availability of data center and colocation infrastructure — compute, storage, network, power, and cooling dependencies — supporting the fleet.
Coordinate with data center operators, colocation providers, and remote-hands teams for physical interventions, maintenance windows, and capacity changes.
Manage hardware fault handling, RMA workflows, and site-level incident response across distributed data center and edge sites.
Coordinate with telecommunications providers, colocation partners, cloud vendors, and infrastructure service providers to resolve service-impacting issues and maintain operational continuity.
3. Incident Management & Response
Serve as incident commander on the hardest escalations, including Sev1/P1 incidents, and drive them to resolution within SLA.
Perform deep diagnosis and root-cause analysis on the running system using logs, metrics, and telemetry.
Diagnose complex issues across:
Network connectivity, routing, NAT/CGNAT, and tunnels
Degraded or intermittent links to field-deployed hardware
Production Kubernetes and Linux platform dependencies at the edge
Assume end-to-end ownership of major incidents, service disruptions, and customer escalations until resolution and formal closure.
Act as the highest operational escalation point within the NOC for complex technical and service- impacting incidents.
Provide timely updates to internal stakeholders, leadership teams, and customers during major incidents and service outages.
4. Standards, Runbooks & Operator Certification
Codify diagnostic procedures, escalation paths, and operational standards that make the NOC repeatable and scalable.
Own the operator-certification layer that qualifies operators to run and support the fleet.
Develop and continuously improve runbooks and operational procedures inherited by L1/L2 teams.
5. Escalation & Coordination
Maintain escalation hygiene: reserve L4 product engineering for genuinely complex issues requiring code or firmware changes.
Clearly define problem scope, business impact, and affected systems when escalating, with supporting logs and evidence.
Facilitate technical communication across engineering and operations teams during major incidents, providing timely stakeholder updates.
6. Continuous Service Improvement
Lead post-incident reviews and drive corrective actions to closure.
Identify recurring incidents and contribute preventive improvements and monitoring optimization.
7. Client & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as a primary technical point of contact for customers, partners, vendors, and internal stakeholders on operational and service-related matters.
Participate in customer meetings, operational reviews, service reviews, and technical discussions as a subject matter expert.
Provide clear, professional, and executive-level communication during major incidents, service disruptions, and operational escalations.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with customer technical teams while driving accountability and service excellence.
8. Leadership & Team Development
Provide technical leadership, mentoring, and guidance to L1 and L2 engineers.
Drive knowledge sharing, operational maturity, and continuous improvement initiatives across the NOC function.
Support the development and maintenance of operator certification programs and competency frameworks.
Participate in recruitment, onboarding, training, and capability development activities as the NOC organization scales.
